extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of journalism, editors, and media organizations in India
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes the Press Council of India’s statutory purpose, functions, composition, powers, limits, and the Council’s normative guidance for ethical journalism (accuracy, fairness, advertising, sensitive topics, complaints procedure) primarily for print media in India.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve freedom of the press and maintain standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Press Council’s vision is to 'Preserve the freedom of the Press' and to 'maintain and improve the standards of newspapers and news agencies in India.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as a watchdog and assist newspapers/news agencies in preserving independence; establish a code of conduct that aligns with high professional standards and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norms of Journalists' Conduct (code of conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive guidelines covering journalistic ethics and standards, accuracy and fairness, right to privacy, professional integrity, advertising guidelines, rules regarding paid news, and standards for covering sensitive topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an ethical framework intended to ensure news, views, comments, and information on public interest topics are presented fairly, accurately, unbiasedly, and respectfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: The press should not publish inaccurate, baseless, misleading, or distorted information; core issues must be reported from all perspectives; unfounded rumors should not be treated as facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News reports from FIRs must specify their source and include the perspective of the affected party. Verification and balanced presentation are required; avoid publishing unverified allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements must be clearly distinguishable from editorial content and must not promote certain products or violate sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publications cannot promote products such as cigarettes, tobacco, alcohol, and other intoxicants. Advertisements must not malign religious sentiments or violate existing laws; editors must ensure ads are separate from editorial matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional ethics for sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible reporting on sensitive topics such as caste, religion, and community references is required; avoid unnecessary identification of individuals by caste/community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should not identify individuals by caste or community if it is not relevant to the story. Exercise caution in reporting on hate speech, communal issues, and other sensitive matters to prevent harm and defamation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors hold final responsibility for all content, including advertisements, and must ensure proper verification, respect for privacy rights, and maintenance of ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must ensure corrections and the right to reply are provided when appropriate. Special care required in investigative journalism; editorial oversight is the last line of accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules regarding paid news
rubrics_metrics.description: There are explicit rules and guidance concerning paid news and its ethical implications for press standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid content must not be represented as independent news; the Council addresses paid news as part of its norms and seeks to curb covert paid reporting (the page references 'paid news' under guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for covering court proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must exercise caution when covering court proceedings to avoid publishing defamatory content or interfering with fair trial concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defamatory content should not be published unless verified and demonstrably in the public interest; special restraints may be needed where legal processes are ongoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functions of the Press Council
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary functions include helping newspapers/news agencies maintain independence; building a code of conduct; ensuring high professional standards; encouraging responsibility and public service; monitoring developments affecting news dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional functions: reviewing foreign assistance to Indian media, studying ownership patterns affecting press independence, undertaking studies on press-related matters, and promoting proper relationships among stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suo-motu cognizance and investigative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council can take up cases on its own initiative and has authority to investigate matters affecting press freedom and ethical violations without a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCI may examine ethical violations suo-motu and conduct hearings/gather evidence within its statutory remit; this is part of its quasi-judicial powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint procedure — complaints by the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Press organizations may file complaints regarding interference with press freedom and must provide full particulars of alleged infringement; the process is time-bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainants should submit detailed particulars to allow inquiry; the process follows timelines and statutory procedures set out by the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint procedure — complaints against the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person can file complaints against ethical violations in the press, but must first write to the editor of the concerned publication and follow specified timelines and documentation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints must be filed within two months for dailies, news agencies and weeklies, and within four months for other publications. Complainant must provide names/addresses of newspapers/news agencies/editors/journalists and include a clipping of the relevant matter (original or self‑attested copy with English translation if in an Indian language). Complaints can also be sent by email to pcibppcomplaint@gmail.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and appointment of the Council
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council is composed of 28 members (20 representatives from the press, 5 from the two Houses of Parliament, and 3 individuals with specialized knowledge) and the Chairperson is customarily a former Supreme Court judge; terms are three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One member is nominated each by the University Grants Commission, the Bar Council of India, and the Sahitya Akademi. Composition rules are statutory and intended to balance press representation and outside expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on PCI powers and jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council cannot impose financial penalties or criminal sanctions; decisions are limited to warnings, admonishments, and censures; it has no criminal jurisdiction and cannot act on matters pending in courts; it is limited to print media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of these limits PCI’s orders are advisory/not financially enforceable; its inability to levy fines or criminal sanctions has led to critiques of limited effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance, enforcement effectiveness and need for reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council has been criticized as a 'toothless tiger' due to limited enforcement powers, case backlogs, long resolution times, and modest substantive action rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites performance metrics (e.g., 2011–2012: 90 adjudications, 54 cases disposed/dismissed/withdrawn, ~30% effectiveness) and notes proposals for reforms such as licensing journalists, strengthening punitive powers, and establishing stronger enforcement mechanisms to address paid news, digital media challenges, and delays.
